# Aakkagam Games

> Free browser-based board games and puzzles rebuilt from ancient game traditions. No sign-up, no download, no ads. Two-player games are hotseat: both players share one screen and pass the device between turns.

Aakkagam Games publishes small, fast web implementations of historic games: an Egyptian race game, a Mesoamerican race game, the three-in-a-row family (three men's morris), and Archimedes' dissection puzzle. Each game is playable at a subpath of https://games.aakkagam.com/.

## Games

- [Patolli](https://games.aakkagam.com/patolli/): The Mesoamerican cross-board race game, for two players on one device. Each player races six counters around a cross of 60 squares, and moves are decided by throwing five beans marked on one face rather than dice: one point per marked face, ten for all five, and no marked face ends the turn. There is no capture. A counter may never land on an occupied square, whether the occupant is the opponent's or the player's own, so every piece is safe wherever it stands and blocking is the whole of the strategy. Eight wedge-marked squares cost double the agreed penalty to land on, and eight rounded squares at the arm tips grant another turn. A piece enters from the player's own central square, each player choosing clockwise or anticlockwise, and after the first piece further pieces enter only on a throw of 1. A piece bears off only by an exact throw onto the last square. First player to bear off all six wins the game and the pot. Rules follow R. C. Bell's reconstruction in Board and Table Games (1960), which is a 60-square game without capture, and differs from the 52-square version with captures described in most popular accounts. A round takes roughly 10 to 20 minutes.
- [Senet](https://games.aakkagam.com/senet/): The ancient Egyptian race game, for two players on one device. Each player races five tokens along 30 squares laid out in three rows on a snaking (boustrophedon) path, and moves are decided by throws of four two-sided casting sticks rather than dice. Six marked houses change the rules mid-race: the House of Second Life (square 15) returns a token to the start, the House of Beauty (26) must be landed on by exact throw, the House of Waters (27) traps a token and can send it back, the Houses of Three and Two Judges (28, 29) release a token only on an exact throw of 3 or 2, and the House of Horus (30) is the exit. A token landing on a lone opponent swaps places with it; two adjacent tokens of one player cannot be taken, and three in a row form a wall that blocks passage. First player to bear off all five tokens wins. Rules follow the reconstruction published by the Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago. A round takes roughly 10 to 20 minutes.
- [align3](https://games.aakkagam.com/align3/): Three men's morris for two players on one device. Each player has three stones on a nine-point board; place them, then slide along the lines until one player aligns all three. Includes two historically distinct variants with different win conditions:
  - Roman circle (Terni Lapilli): win on any of 4 spokes through the center, or any 3 consecutive rim points. Based on the game whose boards are scratched into Roman ruins.
  - Tamil square (kattam): win only on the 8 straight lines of a 3×3 grid (rows, columns, diagonals). Based on the Tamil pebble game drawn as a grid in the sand.
- [ostomachion](https://games.aakkagam.com/ostomachion/): Archimedes' 14-piece square dissection puzzle (also called the stomachion or loculus of Archimedes) for one player. Scramble the pieces, then rebuild the square; there are 17,152 distinct solutions, a count settled by mathematicians in 2003. Archimedes wrote a treatise on it, one of the earliest known mathematical studies of a puzzle; it survives partly in the Archimedes Palimpsest.

## Key facts

- All games are free, ad-free, and require no account.
- Games run entirely in the browser (mobile and desktop) and save progress only to the device.
- Senet, Patolli and align3 are local hotseat play for exactly 2 players; ostomachion is a solo puzzle.
- Senet is a race game of partial chance, and differs from backgammon in three ways: a single snaking track of 30 squares rather than 24 points, four casting sticks rather than dice, and marked houses that alter the rules mid-race.
- Three men's morris differs from tic-tac-toe: with only three pieces per player, play continues after placement with sliding moves, so games don't stall into automatic draws.
